fatal_errors: The proposed ALD/La-doped CeO2-ZrO2 intervention does not reconstruct the target's closed-loop high-throughput discovery of aged multielement alloy catalysts.

The cited evidence concerns Pd nanoparticles on La-Ce-Zr-Al mixed oxides for methane oxidation; it does not establish ALD of Pt, atomically dispersed Pt, vacancy anchoring, reduced Pt loading, or performance in multicomponent automotive exhaust.
The experiment changes deposition method, La doping, and potentially Pt loading simultaneously, so it cannot identify which factor causes any improvement.
The falsification rule is conjunctive and permits the hypothesis to survive failure of an essential claim, such as no durability gain or no reduction in required Pt loading.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested application and offers a scientifically plausible alternative based on dispersion and metal-support interactions. However, it is far from the hidden target, which used Bayesian and inverse-model-guided exploration of five- to nineteen-element alloys on La-doped gamma-Al2O3 and evaluated activity after a specified 900 °C lean/rich ageing protocol. The proposed conditions and outcomes are not quantified by feed composition, ageing severity, light-off metrics, loading reduction, or an objective success threshold. Its baseline is confounded because both support composition and deposition method differ. The supporting paper provides only indirect evidence that La-containing ceria-zirconia mixed oxides can improve oxygen mobility and thermal stability of Pd catalysts; it does not support the central Pt-ALD single-atom mechanism. A discriminating test would compare ALD and impregnation at identical Pt loading on the same La-doped support, include undoped-support controls, apply a defined multicomponent exhaust and ageing protocol, and prespecify activity-retention and PGM-saving thresholds.
